import pandas as pd


def run(inputs: dict[str, "pd.DataFrame"]) -> dict[str, "pd.DataFrame"]:
    events = inputs["events"].copy()

    # Ensure proper dtype for timestamp ordering/arithmetic
    events["event_ts"] = pd.to_datetime(events["event_ts"])

    # Order within (user_id, channel): event_ts, then event_id (tie-break)
    df = events.sort_values(
        by=["user_id", "channel", "event_ts", "event_id"],
        kind="mergesort",
    ).reset_index(drop=True)

    grp_keys = ["user_id", "channel"]

    # Previous event timestamp within the SAME (user_id, channel) stream
    prev_ts = df.groupby(grp_keys, sort=False)["event_ts"].shift(1)

    gap_seconds = (df["event_ts"] - prev_ts).dt.total_seconds()

    # Strict 25-minute gap rule: a new session starts if there is no
    # previous event in this (user_id, channel) stream, OR the gap exceeds
    # 25 minutes (1500 seconds) strictly.
    new_session = gap_seconds.isna() | (gap_seconds > 1500)

    df["_new_session"] = new_session.astype(int)

    # 1-based session number per (user_id, channel), reset for each group
    df["session_num"] = df.groupby(grp_keys, sort=False)["_new_session"].cumsum()

    sessions = (
        df.groupby(["user_id", "channel", "session_num"], sort=False)
        .agg(
            session_start=("event_ts", "min"),
            session_end=("event_ts", "max"),
            event_count=("event_id", "count"),
        )
        .reset_index()
    )

    sessions = sessions.sort_values(
        by=["user_id", "channel", "session_num"], kind="mergesort"
    ).reset_index(drop=True)

    sessions["session_num"] = sessions["session_num"].astype("int64")
    sessions["event_count"] = sessions["event_count"].astype("int64")

    return {"channel_sessions": sessions}
